caption: WER during fine-tuning Whisper model with different types of fine-tunning
model_annotation: The plot titled “Whisper fine-tunning, type = full” illustrates how word error rate (WER) changes over training epochs for two Whisper model variants during fine-tuning, with both series shown on the same axes. The x-axis is labeled “epoch,” uses a linear scale, and runs from 0 to 6 with integer tick marks at every 1 epoch. The y-axis is labeled “WER,” uses a linear scale, and spans roughly from about 19 to 29, with labeled ticks at regular 2-unit intervals (20, 22, 24, 26, 28). One line labeled “tiny full” is drawn in gray with a dotted style and upward-pointing triangle markers; it starts near 28.9 at epoch 0, decreases to about 27.3 at epoch 1 and ~26.9 at epoch 2, drops to about 24.1 at epoch 3, stays around 24.0 at epoch 4, then declines to ~23.5 at epoch 5 and ends near 22.9 at epoch 6. The second line labeled “base full” is drawn in blue with a dotted style and upward-pointing triangle markers; it begins around 21.9 at epoch 0, moves to about 20.9 at epoch 1 and ~21.3 at epoch 2, then decreases to ~20.5 at epoch 3, ~19.7 at epoch 4, ~19.4 at epoch 5, and ends around 19.0 at epoch 6.
